outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Crypto resilience heading into Fed week
strongest.reason: Bitcoin (+~1% to $65.1K) and Ethereum (+~3% to $1,935) both firmed up over the past day, continuing to hold up better than the choppier tech-equity tape as the market heads into Wednesday's Fed decision.

strongest.area: AI-infrastructure and enterprise-software names showing pre-market strength
strongest.reason: Broadcom (+2.6%) and Microsoft (+1.5% pre-market ahead of its July 29 earnings) firmed up, while Vishay Precision Group (+5.9%) and Cadence extended their bounces — a broad enough set of gainers to look like more than one-off moves.

weakest.area: Memory chips & AI hardware supply chain
weakest.reason: Micron fell further to about $921 (down almost 7%), pushing the stock near bear-market territory as the Korea-led memory rout (SK Hynix, Samsung) extends into a second week; Ouster gave back its recent bounce (-8.1%) and Arm remains down over 8% from its post-earnings drop, with SK Hynix's July 29 earnings the next test.

Palantir extended its pullback (-7.1%) on continued NHS-contract scrutiny ahead of its August 3 earnings, while Oracle and Synopsys are still working through the AI-capex-return and EDA-disruption debates that have weighed on them for weeks.

outlook.nextStep: Oil's roughly 7.7% plunge on the weekend's US-Iran de-escalation is lifting futures into Wednesday's Fed decision — worth watching closely rather than acting on, since the meeting itself is the real catalyst and markets are still split on the outcome. Micron's slide toward bear-market territory paired with ASML's guidance raise is the more textured, worth-a-closer-look signal in chips; Palantir's fresh pressure ahead of its August 3 print is better watched for confirmation than acted on now.

signals.title: Oil tumbles ~7.7% as US-Iran tensions ease, Fed decision looms Wednesday
signals.body: WTI crude fell to about $83.51 (Brent fell a similar ~7.7% to around $89.41) as the weekend pause in US-Iran hostilities rapidly deflated the war-risk premium built up over recent weeks. The move helped lift S&P 500 futures (+0.9%) and Nasdaq-100 futures (+1.4%) heading into Monday's open, with the Fed's July 28-29 meeting now just two days away; pricing currently shows roughly a two-thirds chance of no change, though some traders are pricing a modest chance of a hike given sticky inflation.
signals.watch: Wednesday's 2pm ET Fed decision and press conference, and whether the Iran ceasefire holds through the week.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a fast-moving geopolitical de-escalation plus a binary Fed decision two days out is a lot of event risk to sit in front of.

signals.title: Micron nears bear-market territory as the memory rout drags into a second week
signals.body: Micron fell further to roughly $921 (down almost 7% on the day), pushing the stock close to bear-market territory as the Korea-led memory selloff (SK Hynix, Samsung) continues to weigh on U.S. names. Some sell-side coverage has framed ASML's recent guidance raise as a signal to view the memory pullback as a buying opportunity rather than a change in the underlying AI-demand story. SK Hynix reports earnings July 29.
signals.watch: SK Hynix's July 29 print for confirmation of whether memory demand is actually cooling, and any read-through to Western Digital or Lam Research.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a stock nearing bear-market territory alongside a specific, dated earnings catalyst is more concrete than last week's vaguer 'AI pullback' framing.

signals.title: Microsoft firms up pre-market ahead of Wednesday's earnings
signals.body: Microsoft was indicated roughly 1.5% higher in pre-market trading Monday, holding up better than the broader Nasdaq-100 heading into its July 29 earnings report — still among Morgan Stanley's highest-conviction AI-software/infrastructure picks. Oracle remains the laggard of the group, still trading near $115 and unresolved on the AI-capex-return debate weighing on cloud peers.
signals.watch: Microsoft's July 29 print, especially Azure and AI-capex commentary, and any fresh analyst repositioning on Oracle.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — pre-market strength ahead of a major print is worth tracking into the actual results.

signals.title: Palantir extends its pullback ahead of August 3 earnings
signals.body: Palantir fell further (down roughly 7% recently), continuing the pressure tied to NHS-contract scrutiny and open-source-rival headlines, with the stock now down noticeably from recent highs heading into its August 3 earnings report.
signals.watch: Any additional NHS or government-contract headlines before the print, and how the options market is pricing the earnings move.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a stock under multi-source pressure heading into an earnings print carries elevated event risk in both directions.

signals.title: Teradyne heads into July 28 earnings after a rough stretch
signals.body: Teradyne remains pressured ahead of its Tuesday earnings report, with roughly 70% of its revenue now tied to AI-related test equipment — making the print a useful read-through for AI-capex spending broadly, not just semiconductor-test demand specifically.
signals.watch: Tuesday's earnings and any commentary on AI-related order trends.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a name this levered to AI capex reporting right after the memory-chip selloff is a useful cross-check on the 'AI slowdown' narrative.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum both firm up heading into Fed week
signals.body: Bitcoin is holding near $65,100 (+~1%) and Ethereum near $1,935 (+~3%), with both continuing to hold up better than the choppier tech-equity tape as the market heads into the Fed decision.
signals.watch: Whether crypto's relative calm persists through the Fed announcement or whether traditional risk-off patterns reassert themselves.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — the recent pattern of crypto decoupling from equity volatility is a data point worth tracking rather than a one-day blip.

signals.title: CrowdStrike strength continues as cybersecurity outperforms broader software
signals.body: CrowdStrike has continued to firm up following its recent 4-for-1 stock split and a strengthened revenue outlook, extending the pattern where cybersecurity names have outperformed the broader enterprise-software group this month. NetApp and Zscaler both ticked modestly higher as well.
signals.watch: Whether the group's relative strength holds through upcoming peer earnings, and any follow-through from the CrowdStrike split.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — this is now a multi-week pattern rather than a single day's move.
